tasks.short: Gather results, absence and placement data, build the tables, write comments on students and activities, check the report, send it to administration, and answer their questions.

steps.what: Technical teacher gathers results, absence and placement data from several systems
Technical teacher builds the report tables in a spreadsheet
Technical teacher prepares written comments on students and activities for the report

loop.input: The teacher's notes per student and activity and the report tables.
loop.output: Draft comments per student and activity.
loop.check: Each sentence must trace to a teacher note or a number in the tables, or it is dropped; the teacher edits and approves the text.
loop.stop: Stops when the teacher approves, or after two redrafts the teacher writes the comments.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments need short prose per student; a template gives the same sentence for everyone.

steps.what: Technical teacher checks the full report
Technical teacher e-mails the report to administration
Technical teacher answers administration's questions about the report

tasks.design: A report query in the student system ({OTHER}) pulls results, absence and placement data into a fixed report template, so the teacher does not copy them into a spreadsheet. A bounded step drafts comments from the teacher's notes; any sentence that does not trace to a note or a number is dropped, and the teacher edits. Once the teacher has checked the report, it goes to administration from the system. Judging students stays with the teacher; the model sets no grade.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were copied from several systems into spreadsheets and comments written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems run report queries; language models draft comments from notes.
tasks.human_edge: Writing about a student fairly when the numbers tell only part of the story.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks and edits reports instead of compiling them.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive complete and on time.

evidence.claim: Student systems hold pupil records from which reports can be queried; a model can draft comments from teacher notes.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk under Annex III point 3, so the model only drafts wording from the teacher's own notes.

assumptions: Boundary: from the report request to questions answered; administration's use of the report is outside.
Input contract: data from the student system; notes by the teacher; fallback is spreadsheets and writing by hand.
Checking the report stays with the teacher.
Student data go only to a model approved in the school's DPIA.
research_questions: How much of the drafted comments does the teacher change?

already_counted.description: Technical teacher edits and approves drafted comments.

incremental.description: Technical teacher updates the report query when formats change.

approvals.approved_version: The report as checked by the teacher in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: reports with mostly free text; high: reports with many tables from student data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the agenda and documents, attend staff meetings, work on committee tasks, take minutes when it is your turn, and share the minutes with the committee.

steps.what: Technical teacher reads the agenda and meeting documents
Technical teacher serves on committees and works on committee tasks
Technical teacher takes the minutes when it is their turn
Technical teacher e-mails the minutes to committee members

tasks.design: Each meeting has one page in the school's document space ({DOCS}) with the agenda, documents and a minutes template with an action list, so documents are not hunted down in e-mail. Once the minute-taker has finished the minutes, committee members see them on the same page. Attending meetings and committee work stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agendas and documents came by e-mail and minutes were formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared meeting pages with templates are common in schools.
tasks.still_hard: Meetings take as long as the discussion needs.
tasks.human_edge: Speaking up for the workshop when budgets are divided.

reach.learn: Whether actions get done between meetings.

evidence.claim: Shared document spaces can hold meeting pages with agenda, documents and minutes templates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting agenda to the minutes shared; decisions by the school board are outside.
Input contract: agendas set by chairs; fallback is e-mail.
Meetings and committee work do not change.
research_questions: Do actions get done between meetings more often?

incremental.description: Technical teacher fills in actions on the meeting page.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes as finished by the minute-taker in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few committees; high: several committees with frequent minutes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise halls and the cafeteria, supervise bus loading and unloading, help in the school library, and check the supervision roster.

steps.what: Technical teacher performs hall and cafeteria monitoring
Technical teacher supervises bus loading and unloading
Students bring books to the library desk to borrow them
Technical teacher provides school library assistance, checking books in and out
Technical teacher checks the paper supervision roster

tasks.design: A self-service lending kiosk in the school library lets students check books in and out with their student card, so the teacher on library duty helps rather than processes loans. The supervision roster sits in the staff calendar ({CALENDAR}) with reminders. Hall, cafeteria and bus supervision stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loans went through the desk and the roster was a paper list in the staff room.
tasks.enabler_now: Library kiosks and staff calendars with reminders are common in schools.
tasks.still_hard: Supervision duties take the time they take.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the student who is alone at lunch every day.

reach.learn: Whether kiosk loans free the desk.

evidence.claim: Library kiosks let students check books in and out with a card.

assumptions: Boundary: from the supervision roster to duties done; the library's collection is outside.
Input contract: roster set by the school office; kiosk run by the librarian; fallback is the desk and paper.
Students check out books at the kiosk in about the time the desk took; priced as customer time.

incremental.description: Technical teacher helps students at the kiosk.
Students check books in and out at the kiosk.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: little library duty; high: frequent library duty with many loans.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technical teacher keeps judging students, meeting colleagues and supervising; copying data, building tables, hunting documents and desk loans shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time with students in the workshop.
